minutes.headline: Select Board appointed three volunteers and heard the APDC on a bylaw appeal article and the old primary school.
minutes.summary: The board appointed two cultural council members and a Green Communities task force member by roll call. It met the Architectural Preservation District Commission about nominating the old primary school to the National Register and Town Meeting article 24 on appeals for town-owned buildings. It also reviewed a Monty Tech concept drawing, the TC Passios design article, the consent calendar, and a COVID update before going to executive session on DPW union bargaining.

what_happened.line: The Select Board appointed Elise Wiley and Karen Kemp to the cultural council by roll call, with all ayes heard on both votes.
The board appointed Matt Snyder to the Green Communities task force by roll call, all ayes heard.

The Architectural Preservation District Commission discussed nominating the old primary school to the National Register; no nomination vote was taken and the commission is to send grant and listing information.
Article 24, on appeals under the architectural preservation bylaw for town-owned buildings, will go to Town Meeting as printed in the warrant, with the board to review the commission's input.

Article 27, a Salary Administration Plan amendment, was pulled from the consent calendar after a Finance Committee member objected; the design article for the old primary site (article 26) still had no dollar amount.

why_it_matters: The old primary school site is moving toward Town Meeting through several articles (a design article, an engineering article, a bylaw appeal change), and residents will be asked to vote on money and rules for it.

Article 24 would change how town-owned buildings are treated under the preservation bylaw, and the article for design work carried no dollar amount at this meeting, so the cost residents are asked to approve was not yet known.
watch_next: The dollar amount for the design article (article 26), expected before the Finance Committee meets on the warrant.
The next Select Board meeting, moved from April 20 to April 27, and Town Meeting votes on articles 24 and 27.

The records diverge on the engineering article, where ours has $30,000 and the official minutes say no amount was available.
